question: Does the test-first asymmetry survive newer models?
body: The key studies are Python-only and predate 2025 frontier models; nobody has re-run TDD-Bench on current models. Vague requirements, where TDD is claimed to earn its keep as a thinking tool, are untested with agents.

question: Is human code review worth its cost?
body: Majors calls review the least valuable part of what humans add and moves trust into tests and production. Honeycomb targets 25% auto-merged PRs at under 3% change failure rate, which can be checked in 2027.

question: What is actually scarce: verification, judgement or understanding?
body: Fornasier and Litt disagree. Both are n=1 or opinion.

question: Do strong engineering foundations protect you?
body: DORA says partly; Faros telemetry says no outcome is protected.

question: Is maintenance capability improving?
body: SWE-CI says fast; SlopCodeBench shows flat decay across model tiers.

question: Do context files help?
body: One study finds time savings; another finds no success gain and 20% more cost. Claude Code was the one agent that developer-written files did not improve.

question: How much upfront specification is right?
body: More supplied tests peaked at two, and agents that designed up front did better, so spec-first may repeat the waterfall fallacy. Others argue the spec is the durable artifact and should be executable, and the agent-TDD study that found no gain told its agents not to design up front.

question: Should planning prompts be looser than execution prompts?
body: One practitioner argues for goals-only planning prompts and fully detailed execution prompts. Opinion with no data.

question: Fresh context each loop, or continued context?
body: Ralph resets every iteration; one comparison found continuing did better per unit cost (n=1 task).

question: Does multi-agent orchestration scale, or does Brooks's Law apply to agents?
Is skill loss reversible, and how do we measure cognitive debt?
body: No accepted measure exists; comprehension gates are untested for durability.

question: Can partial theory be enough?
body: Naur says a team's theory can't be revived from docs; Goedecke argues most engineers work fine on partial theory.

question: Will prompt injection ever have a real fix?
body: Guardrails that stop 95% of attacks are a failing grade by security standards. Should the writing agent ever approve its own PR, as Anthropic reportedly aims for?

question: How do juniors become seniors?
body: Entry-level hiring shrinks and questions go to the model rather than to colleagues.

question: Can agents keep their own project memory current?
body: The maker of a markdown memory tool says agents keep documentation current when the update is built into every task, yet admits he still trims it by hand. Other sources say agents don't clean up after themselves, and models handle stale facts poorly.
